assumptions.obligation: i_full_thr is static: once both domains are out of hardware reset, it stays the same at every i_clk_wr edge (written once before use, not changed while the FIFO is in use).
i_empty_thr is static: once both domains are out of hardware reset, it stays the same at every i_clk_rd edge (written once before use, not changed while the FIFO is in use).
No write request (i_wr_en = 0) at any i_clk_wr edge while i_rst_n_wr or i_rst_n_rd is asserted: no FIFO operation starts before both domains have left reset.
No read request (i_rd_en = 0) at any i_clk_rd edge while i_rst_n_rd or i_rst_n_wr is asserted: no FIFO operation starts before both domains have left reset.

notes:
The constraints are kept small on purpose. Nothing below is constrained, because the specification calls all of it legal: writing while full or reading while empty (these must raise overflow or underflow pulses), accesses during a software reset (they must be blocked with no error pulse), i_rst_n_sw going low for one or more cycles at any time (including while o_sw_rst_busy = 1 or in REL), any i_wr_data value, any threshold value (AF-20.2-05/06), and resets that are not asserted at the same time.

Some obligations from the specification could not be written under the coding rules (immediate assumptions clocked only by i_clk_wr or i_clk_rd, with no global clock):
(a) i_wr_en, i_wr_data, i_rst_n_sw and i_rd_en change only at rising edges of their own clock (AF-10.6.2-09, AF-10.7.4-01). Changes between edges are allowed. They only matter for combinational glitches on o_full and the threshold flags, so clocked checks are not affected.
(b) Each reset stays low for at least one edge of its own clock and is released synchronously (AF-6.2-03, AF-3-34, AF-20.1-01). Only the initial reset is guaranteed by the setup.
(c) These are liveness rules and cannot be written as clocked safety assumptions: i_rst_n_sw must eventually return to 1 (AF-11.2-03, AF-6.2-11), and both clocks must keep running during the software reset (AF-20.1-06). A bounded-completion check such as AF-15.3-15 needs a fairness bound that the specification does not give.
(d) AF-12-07 says the integrator must reset both domains. This is only partly covered: ENV-03/04 keep traffic idle while either reset is active. It is not forced that a reset of one domain is always followed by a reset of the other, because AF-3-36 and AF-7.2-11 say the resets are independent. A trace that resets only one domain can therefore fail the pointer-consistency checks, which the specification says the IP does not repair (AF-7.2-12).

Parameter legality is a configuration matter and is not written here as input assumptions. The rules are: depth a power of 2 and at least 2, data width at least 1, PARA_AFIFO_CELL_TYPE from 1 to 4, and not 0 on the pointer crossings (AF-3-23, AF-14.4-06, AF-8-04..14). The formal run should choose legal values, for example the default CELL_TYPE = 2.
